name: Kyzart Pass
dist: On the highway between the Kochkor and Jumgal districts
near: The village of Kyzart (Jumgal district, population 1516 in 2021) — about 14 km southwest of the pass, at the descent into the Jumgal valley; Kochkor is the base for trips (~55–60 km along the highway, estimate); Chayek is the Jumgal district center.
elev: 2664 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, Nomad's Land, Wikipedia, Knews).
short: A year-round road pass (2664 m) on the EM-18 highway (formerly A-367) Kochkor–Chayek between the Kochkor and Jumgal valleys; the starting point of horse routes to Song-Kol and the famous roadside trailers selling fried peled (whitefish).
desc: Kyzart is a modest pass between the Kum-Bel and Baba-Ata ranges on the international EM-18 highway (formerly A-367), which leads from Kochkor into the Jumgal valley, to Chayek and on toward Suusamyr. The eastern slope is gentle, the western is steep; the pass is open year-round, although in winter there is strong wind and snow here. The folk name is “Maiden Pass”: according to local legend, forty girls died of cold here. At a small parking area next to a mosque, blue trailer cafes serve only fried peled from Lake Song-Kol, bread and tea. In summer yurts stand around, and the pass itself and the village of the same name are the main starting points of horse and hiking trips by CBT Kochkor and local herders to Song-Kol via the Kyzyl-Kiya jailoo (summer pasture), Chaar-Archa Pass (3061 m), the Kilemche jailoo (summer pasture) and Jalgyz-Karagai Pass (3400 m).
guide: Stop at Kyzart for lunch — in the blue trailers by the mosque they fry peled from Song-Kol (100–150 som a fish in 2019), and tea is poured without limit. If you are riding to Song-Kol, clarify exactly where you meet: CBT Kochkor gathers groups at the pass itself, while private horse handlers and Horseback Holiday meet in the village of Kyzart, 14 km lower. Haggle: according to 2025 reviews, the price of a horse tour for two in the village was brought down from 15,000 to 10,000 som. In winter the pass is open, but the wind here is piercing — don't plan a long stop.
see: A view of the Kochkor and Jumgal valleys; trailer cafes with fried peled by the mosque; summer yurts; the start of horse trails to Song-Kol (Kyzyl-Kiya, Chaar-Archa 3061 m, Kilemche); Mount Baba-Ata on the way.
skip: You are not going to Jumgal or riding to Song-Kol — the pass itself is low, more a point on the highway than a destination in its own right. You don't eat fish. You want dramatic serpentines — there are more of them on Moldo-Ashuu.
diff: Easy for a car: a paved road with occasional gravel sections (Knews, 2019), open year-round. The horse/hiking route to Song-Kol is moderate: 2 passes above 3000–3400 m, 4–6 h a day (CBT Kochkor); on foot ~60 km in 3 days.
when: As transit — year-round (Nomad's Land, Wikipedia). For horse treks to Song-Kol — mid-June to the end of September (CBT Kochkor); yurts on the route — mid-June to early September.
hours: The highway is open year-round. Trailer cafes — hours not published (they work in season and by day, and per a 2019 review in autumn as well).
daytime: By day: in winter and the off-season ice and wind are possible in the morning; in season, lunch in the trailer cafes. For the start of a horse route — early in the morning (5–6 h of travel).
how: Along the EM-18 highway from Kochkor west toward Chayek: Kochkor → Kyzart Pass (~55–60 km, ~1 h; estimate) → descent to the village of Kyzart and into the Jumgal valley (Jumgal is 68 km from Kochkor per Nomad's Land). From Bishkek: Bishkek–Balykchy–Kochkor–Kyzart, ~260 km (estimate). From the south, from Song-Kol — on horseback via Jalgyz-Karagai and Kilemche.
needcar: For the pass — a car/taxi/marshrutka (minibus) toward Chayek. For the horse route — a transfer Kochkor → the pass/the village of Kyzart, then a horse.
self: Yes: the pass is on an open highway, no permits. The hiking trek to Song-Kol can be done independently with offline maps (no markings); a horse — only with a guide.
roadtype: International highway EM-18: paved with gravel sections (Knews, 2019); the eastern climb is gentle, the western descent to the village of Kyzart is steep. From the pass/village to Kilemche — horse and foot trails, not roads.
traveltime: Kochkor — the pass ~1 h (estimate); Bishkek — Kyzart ~4–4.5 h. Horse route: Kyzart Pass → Kilemche 4–5 h on horseback (5–6 h on foot), Kilemche → Song-Kol ~5 h on horseback (CBT Kochkor); on foot 18 + 18 + 24 km in 3 days (elprismadefer).
stay: Yurts at the pass in summer (Nomad's Land); Trip to Kyrgyzstan mentions guesthouses in the area. On the horse route: a CBT yurt camp at Kilemche — 1500 som without meals / 2000 som with dinner and breakfast; a yurt at Song-Kol — 1500–2000 som with breakfast/dinner (2024–2025). In the village of Kyzart — a homestay with horse handlers (Horseback Holiday), prices on request.
net: Not confirmed by sources for the saddle; on the Kochkor–Chayek highway and in the villages there is a signal (operators not named). On the horse route above Kyzyl-Kiya there is no signal — offline maps are essential.
entry: Free: the pass is on an open highway, no fees.
transfer: Kochkor — Kyzart: 350–400 som/seat shared (2025), a private car 3000 som; Kyzart — Kochkor back 3000 som per car (elprismadefer); Bishkek — Kochkor 350 som (May 2026).
bring: A windproof jacket (strong wind on the pass), cash for fish and tea; for a horse trek — a sleeping bag, rain jacket, sun protection, offline maps (Maps.me/Gaia GPS), water.
warn: The road pass and the village of Kyzart (the start of some horse treks) are different points 14 km apart: clarify the meeting place. In winter wind, snow and ice on the highway. Prices from private horse handlers in Kyzart are inflated — haggle and fix the terms in advance (TripAdvisor, May 2025; brokennavigation 2025).
food: Fried peled from Song-Kol in the blue trailers by the mosque on the pass — 100 som (small) / 150 som (large), tea without limit (Knews, autumn 2019; 2025–2026 prices not confirmed). On the route — kumys from herders, dinner in yurts.
reviews: Google Maps (“Pereval Kyzart”): 5/5, 2 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor on the Kyzart — Song-Kol routes: pros — beautiful pastures and passes, hospitality; cons — difficulties with transport from Kyzart and attempts to inflate the price (May 2025). No separate TripAdvisor page for the pass was found.
p.sum: Kyzart (2664 m) is a paved-and-gravel pass on the Kochkor–Chayek highway, passable year-round: ≈55 km (≈1 h) from Kochkor, and 14 km lower is the village of Kyzart, the main start of hiking and horse trips to Song-Kol via Kilemche. Getting there: marshrutka (minibus) No. 541 “Chayek” from Bishkek or a shared taxi from Kochkor (350–400 som/seat, 2025). A 3-day horse tour with local guides costs 15–20 thousand som/person (2025); there is a marked trail “Starry Song Kul Nights”.
